body: Two new relied rows in the capability ledger, harness prompt prefixes and the R8 identity floor, each with a viola verify probe: every dependence on an undocumented claude behaviour is a ledger row with a verify probe.

The harness-prefix probe: a second session sends into a verify child and the prompt's raw start is read to tell the harness-origin prefix; a harness prompt is never a human turn and never moves the wheel.
The identity-floor probe: environment names, never values, are captured; no value may reach any file, fixture, stamp, log line or screen, and a failing test proves a captured value is refused.
The hidden hook --capture arm of viola verify and its closed set of capture ids, which the new probes may extend.
viola verify --record and its scrub, including the handling of a captured environment name that itself carries private text.
The viola verify output: each new probe's step line and the verified count it adds, printed as plain linear output with no spinner and no SGR off a terminal.
An interrupted viola verify run still keeps its exit and its stderr pair with the new probes in its child set.
The verify stamp's relied-id set and count, stamped from a live run in the rig's scratch home; live readings never gate CI.
The fake agent replays the new probes from the recorded fixture set in CI, so the CI gate holds them without a live claude.
Indirect, through the probe reading the child's prompt: the boundary check never inspects claude content beyond its signatures; only the raw prefix is read.
Indirect, through anything the probes print: C0 and C1 control characters in a captured name or prompt start are printed escaped, never raw.
Indirect, through the probe's run diagnostics and log lines: diagnostics never reach the terminal, and log identity tags stay as they are; no environment value is logged.
Indirect, through any refusal or failure the new probes report: the refusal or failure word comes with its reason code and hint, never a stack trace or bare status, and is never coloured.
Indirect, through the probe's wait on the verify child: time bounds fall on the driver, never on the human.

The harness-prefix row rests on the rule that harness prompts are classified by raw prefix before any unwrapping or un-escaping, and that a harness prompt is no human take and never moves the wheel; the prefix set stays compiled literals.

The identity-floor row rests on the R8 parent-identity floor: eleven named CLAUDE identity variables are always stripped from the child's environment whatever claude_env_keep keeps, and the strip reads names only.

The harness-prefix probe adds a second session sending into a verify child; it must stay inside verify's bounded child set and runs, the Run order verify keeps, and verify's rule that it never types into a CLI dialog; how the second session reaches the child is open to P3.

The identity-floor probe captures environment variable names, never values, through the hidden hook --capture arm or a probe of its kind; capture arms stay inert outside verify, their closed ids and payload-file shape bind any new capture.

No environment value may reach any file, fixture, stamp, log line or screen read; the chunk owes a failing test proving a captured value is refused, and the process-start line of the claude child keeps reporting kept and stripped names only.

The ledger stamps envelope gains the new rows: verify is the sole stamps writer, a merge replaces only its own version, and a version is verified only when every relied row counts, so adding relied rows makes an older, shorter stamp read unverified.

body: viola verify gains two steps, one for each new relied row. Each step prints the verify step line in its fixed form, and a failure prints the failing-row form.
The viola verify summary and summary line count the two new relied rows, and so do the exit-0 and exit-1 outcomes they report.
viola verify --record writes the new probes' captures into the recorded fixture set through its scrub. The --record output reports what it recorded.
viola verify refuses a recorded fixture that is not clean. A captured environment value, or a name that carries private text, must never get past the scrub into a fixture.
viola verify output stays plain ASCII. No environment value and no compiled screen literal from a probe ever reaches stdout or stderr.
Hints never quote text or name paths. Any new verify hint or refusal for the new rows names the next verb only and never quotes an environment name's value or a prompt prefix.
Human output is a contract. The wording of the new verify step lines is fixed and is held by the existing verify output checks.
Results go to stdout and everything else goes to stderr. The new verify steps follow the same split as the existing ones.

The viola verify refusals stay reachable with the new probes in place: CLI not found, CLI version unreadable, viola home not private and verify stopped. The stop output keeps its form when a stop lands during a new probe.
The viola verify --help paragraph and usage still describe what verify does once the two new probes exist.

body: Two new relied capability-ledger rows, each with a viola verify probe, under the universal invariant that every dependence on an undocumented claude behaviour is a ledger row with a verify probe. The stamp's relied-id set and the relied-row count grow with them.

The harness prompt prefixes: the four raw-start literals compiled into the product, harness prompts filed as not human, and a harness turn that never moves the wheel. The probe reads a prompt's raw start against these literals only.
The R8 identity floor: the eleven-name floor stays eleven names. Parent identity variables and inherited CLAUDE credentials are stripped from the child, and the strip reads names only.

Env names never values: the identity-floor probe may capture variable names only. No CLAUDE value is ever serialised, logged, stamped, written to a fixture or shown on a screen, and verification output carries no identity value. A failing test proves that a captured value is refused.

verify's runs and child set: the new probe child is spawned directly, verify never answers or types into a dialog, and it reads the PTY screen only by signatures against compiled literals, with bounded output caught.

The second session sending into a verify child: whatever process sends (a viola endpoint, the channel or a paste, which is P3's call) sends only synthetic probe prompts. Probe effects stay in the probe's own directory, and probe directories and captures are transient and removed.
The hidden hook capture arm: it answers only from closed probe ids, so any new probe id joins that closed set. The capture arms stay isolated from the product paths.

verify --record and its scrub: recorded fixtures are scrubbed or refused whole under the unclean-fixture refusal codes (absolute-path, home-path, username, email), and the refusal line keeps its form. A captured env name that itself carries private text must be handled by the scrub.
The recorded fixture set under the per-version claude fixtures folder (2.1.328, 2.1.329 or both, left to P3 and the founder): only signature rows are kept, and fixtures are reviewed before commit.
